column1: # Organic Maps translation glossary — source of truth for DeepL glossaries.
# Lines starting with # are comments. Blank lines are ignored.
# Use them from any script with:
#     gid = get_glossary_id("ru")   # pass as glossary_id= to /v2/translate
# Mined from the site's own proofread translations with tmp/glossary_extract.py,
# which aligns English news posts line-by-line with each translation and scores
# target tokens by keyness. An entry is included only when the corpus evidence
# is unambiguous, or when CLAUDE.md mandates the term. Terms with split or
# contradictory evidence are listed under NEEDS NATIVE REVIEW at the bottom and
# deliberately left out — a missing entry is safe, a wrong one is not.
# Sources are lowercase: DeepL matches case-insensitively and preserves the
# casing of the surrounding text. Singular and plural are separate entries so
# the target lands in the right number; DeepL inflects for case in context.
# track -> trasa is mandated by CLAUDE.md; the corpus drifted to "takelis".
# DeepL glossaries are keyed by base language code, so pt and pt-BR may not be
# able to coexist. deepl_glossary.py verifies this at sync time and reports it.
# bookmark -> метка and track -> трек are mandated by CLAUDE.md (not закладка).
# bookmark -> мітка and map -> мапа are mandated by CLAUDE.md.
# Languages DeepL glossaries do not support — surfaced via get_review_terms()
# Mined from the same corpus as the rest. DeepL cannot enforce these, so they
# are guidance for the proofreading pass rather than substitutions.
# REPAIRS — post-translation fixes, applied to the OUTPUT text
# These are not terminology; they are known translator defects. Apply with
# ru метek: DeepL corrupts the genitive plural of the glossary term "метки",
# emitting Cyrillic "мет" + LATIN "ek". Confirmed reproducible, glossary-only
# (clean without it), Russian-only — Ukrainian's identical genitive plural
# "міток" is unaffected. Supplying "меток" as the entry avoids this but then
# breaks the prepositional ("метах" for "метках"), so the correct entries are
# kept and the output is repaired instead.
# NEEDS NATIVE REVIEW — deliberately NOT in the glossary above
# 1. track / route collapse — RESOLVED for ar, cs, el and now he
#    Re-measured against the lines where the English mentions BOTH senses,
#    which is where a language that distinguishes them has to show it:
#        ar  المسارات المسجلة والإشارات المرجعية ومسارات التنقل
#        cs  Záznamy tras, záložky a plánované trasy
#    Each distinguishing term appears in 0 of the route-only lines, so the
#    three candidates are confirmed and now entered above:
#        ar المسار المسجل (8)   cs stopa (10)   el ίχνος (46)
#    Hebrew was genuinely collapsed — מסלול covered 105 of 115 track lines
#    AND 86 of 93 route lines — and is now settled by native review rather
#    than by corpus evidence, because the corpus had none to give.
#    Hebrew has no pair of single words that reproduces the distinction, and
#    forcing one produces worse Hebrew than qualifying the shared noun. So
#    מסלול stays the word for both senses and the sense is carried by a
#        navigation route מסלול ניווט      (only when contrasted with tracks)
#        recorded track   מסלול מוקלט      (only when known to be recorded)
#        the line itself  תוואי / תוואי המסלול
#    `track` is entered as מסלול GPS rather than מסלול מוקלט on purpose: GPX
#    permits a <trk> that was drawn, imported or simplified rather than
#    recorded, so מוקלט would assert something untrue of it. Reserve מוקלט
#    for tracks the app itself recorded.
#    Rejected, with reasons: נתיב reads as a traffic lane and would collide
#    with lane guidance; עקבה is forensic-sounding and unpointed is
#    indistinguishable from the place name Aqaba; רצועה is a strip or media
#    track; טרק is a hiking trip; מסילה is a railway; שביל is a physical
#    trail, which a GPS track need not follow; מעקב is the act of tracking,
#    Grammar for proofreading: מסלול and תוואי are masculine (מסלולים,
#    תוואים). Note המסלול המוקלט ("the recorded track") against המסלול מוקלט
#    ("the track is recorded"), and the construct הקלטת מסלול — never
#    The disagreement came from measuring the news posts alone. Over the whole
#    corpus الإشارات المرجعية leads 37 to 15, agreeing with the earlier
#    release-note review, so it is canonical.
# 3. Split evidence, no clear winner — omitted
#    it crash   kept as "crash" (13) / arresto anomalo (5)
#    pt track   trilho (11) / percurso (6)  — trilho entered, worth confirming
#    hu track recording  "útvonalrögzítés" uses útvonal (route), not nyomvonal
#    pt track — three competing terms, no winner:
#        news posts  trilho (39)      FAQ pages  trilhas (4)
#        the app itself uses percurso, and uses it for "route" as well
#        ("Quer recalcular o percurso?" and "Gravação de percurso"), so the
#        product collapses the two senses in European Portuguese.
#        `trilho` is entered above on the news evidence; a native speaker
#        should decide whether the site should follow the app instead.
#    ja — only one translated news post on the site, too little to align.
#    oc bookmark — corpus is split, marcapaginas (12) vs marcadors (5). The
#    first is the book sense, the second the map-marker sense the project uses
#    elsewhere; omitted until a native speaker settles it.
#    eu crash — hutsegitea (4) vs kraskadura (4), no winner.
#    eu track — the corpus keeps the English word in some files and uses
#    ibilbide (route) in others, collapsing the two senses.
#    Languages DeepL glossaries do not support at all, needing local
#    substitution instead: af, ca, cy, eu, fa-IR, gl, hi, ml, mr, oc, te
# 5. Excluded English terms — ambiguous in the corpus, unsafe to force
#    steps  ("these steps will vary" vs stairs)
#    note   ("Please note that" vs OSM note)
#    style  ("a song in a different style" vs map style)
#    recording ("recording of the Zoom session" vs track recording)
#    search (high frequency, noun/verb ambiguity across languages)
# BRAND LOCK — keep product names Latin while still VISIBLE to the translator
# Hiding brands behind <x> placeholders wrecks word order: the translator
# cannot see them, so "OpenStreetMap data as of August 4" came back as
# "OpenStreetMap Теперь включены данные…" in ~30 of 32 languages. Leaving them
# visible fixes the word order, and these identity entries stop DeepL
# transliterating them (أندرويد, אנדרואיד). Languages with no glossary support
# (hi, ml, te, fa-IR …) keep placeholder protection instead — see BRAND_VISIBLE
